readme: Golden question set for retrieval. `expect` lists the concept ids that answer the question — a hit on any of them counts, so a question with two legitimate answers is not penalized for picking either. `conflict` asserts that resolving the concept surfaces dissent from the named layers, which is the thing ContextCake claims to do that a flat wiki cannot. `probes` records why the question is in the set; when a question starts passing or failing, that note is what tells you whether the change was real.

questions.question: what language should I use for a new service?
questions.probes: natural phrasing with stopwords; three layers disagree and all three must survive

questions.question: which database do we use for service state?
questions.probes: direct lexical match on a distinctive term

questions.question: what databases are we allowed to use?
questions.probes: plural form of a term the corpus writes in the singular

questions.question: where should analytics queries run?
questions.probes: team overrides the org answer; the org position must still be visible

questions.question: how do I store secrets?
questions.probes: short natural question, single strong term

questions.question: what TLS version is required?
questions.probes: acronym plus a common noun

questions.question: how long do we keep logs?
questions.probes: the doc says retained, the question says keep — no lexical overlap on the verb

questions.question: how long are customer records retained?
questions.probes: same concept as q07 with the document's own vocabulary, to isolate vocabulary effects

questions.question: when does a Sev1 page someone?
questions.probes: distinctive token that appears in exactly one document

questions.question: do we need a postmortem for a Sev2?
questions.probes: two distinctive tokens, both in the same document

questions.question: how do I get production access?
questions.probes: production also appears in deploy, observability and security docs

questions.question: how many approvals does a pull request need?
questions.probes: the corpus says change and review, never pull request

questions.question: who reviews changes to billing code?
questions.probes: reviews vs review — morphological variant of the key term

questions.question: how do I roll back a bad deploy?
questions.probes: roll back vs rollback — tokenization boundary

questions.question: can I deploy on a Friday afternoon?
questions.probes: team explicitly reverses the org rule; both answers must be present

questions.question: what are the deployment windows?
questions.probes: deployment vs deploys — morphological variant

questions.question: what metrics should my service export?
questions.probes: streaming metrics override request metrics; the org list must still show

questions.question: how should I paginate a collection endpoint?
questions.probes: paginate vs pagination — morphological variant

questions.question: how do we version breaking API changes?
questions.probes: version and breaking both appear in schema-evolution as a distractor

questions.question: why are my Spark executors getting killed?
questions.probes: executors vs executor; killed appears in the target document

questions.question: executor exit code 137 during a join
questions.probes: keyword-style query pasted from an error, no natural language

questions.question: how do we handle skewed join keys?
questions.probes: skewed vs skew — morphological variant on the decisive term

questions.question: my consumer group keeps rebalancing after a deploy
questions.probes: rebalancing vs rebalance; deploy is a strong distractor term

questions.question: how do I stop rebalance storms?
questions.probes: exact title vocabulary — should be the easiest question in the set

questions.question: how should Kafka topics be named?
questions.probes: named vs naming/names — morphological variant

questions.question: should I partition by timestamp?
questions.probes: the answer is a warning against the thing asked about

questions.question: do we use exactly-once delivery?
questions.probes: hyphenated term; tokenizer keeps hyphens so exactly-once splits differently than expected

questions.question: can I rename a field in an Avro schema?
questions.probes: rename vs renaming; field appears across many documents

questions.question: which schema changes are backward compatible?
questions.probes: compatible vs compatibility — morphological variant

questions.question: the pipeline is stalled, what do I do?
questions.probes: heavy stopword load around two content words

questions.question: consumer lag is growing overnight
questions.probes: genuinely two-answer question; either is a correct first hit

questions.question: how do I run a backfill safely?
questions.probes: distinctive term, but run appears everywhere

questions.question: can I reuse the checkpoint when reprocessing?
questions.probes: checkpoint appears in three documents; reprocessing only in the target

questions.question: how do I run the pipeline on my laptop?
questions.probes: laptop appears once; pipeline appears in six documents

questions.question: kafka advertised listener localhost problem
questions.probes: keyword query where the strongest term is in a low-priority personal note

questions.question: how do I bucket timestamps in ClickHouse?
questions.probes: timestamps vs timestamp; bucket vs bucketing/buckets

questions.question: approximate distinct count in ClickHouse
questions.probes: the document says approximate and uniq, never distinct count

questions.question: why is my ClickHouse query slow?
questions.probes: query and slow both appear in the target; ClickHouse also appears in two team docs

questions.question: what should I check before shipping a new service?
questions.probes: graph prior: production-readiness is a hub linked from six other concepts (new-service-onboarding, service-ownership, on-call-handoff, service-launch-approval, dashboard-conventions, service-decommission); pre-launch-checklist is a lexically similar leaf nothing links to. Today the leaf outranks the hub: rank 4, beaten by pre-launch-checklist, standards/code-review, decisions/data-storage. A graph prior should pull the six-times-linked hub back above the unlinked leaf.

questions.question: is there a checklist to run through before launch?
questions.probes: graph prior: same hub-vs-leaf pair as q39 with checklist-flavored phrasing that plays to the leaf's title and heading vocabulary. Today the hub is rank 3, beaten by pre-launch-checklist and service-launch-approval.

questions.question: what do I need to confirm before a new service ships?
questions.probes: graph prior: another generic pre-launch phrasing where the hub is right but the unlinked leaf's own 'confirm the X, confirm the Y' checklist wording matches more literally. Today the hub is rank 2, immediately behind pre-launch-checklist — a close race a graph signal should tip the hub's way.

questions.question: when is the Tuesday Launch Review meeting?
questions.probes: control question for the hub prior: the leaf is the genuinely correct answer here (the Tuesday Launch Review detail lives only in pre-launch-checklist, not the hub). Today this is rank 1 for the leaf, as it should be — a future graph-prior change must not blindly promote the six-times-linked hub over a leaf that is specifically right.

questions.question: how long before a lock is killed and rolled back automatically?
questions.probes: section-level retrieval: the answer (lock_timeout of 45 seconds, auto-rollback) sits in the 7th of 9 sections of a ~275-token runbook, more than 3x the corpus's average document length, so BM25's length normalization already discounts it. Today it still ranks 1st but by a thin margin (score 6.31) over runbooks/deploy-standard (5.16), whose Rollback section shares 'rolled back'/'automatically' vocabulary — a close race that a per-section scorer should widen rather than flip.

questions.question: does a big change need someone else's approval before it merges?
questions.probes: section-level retrieval: the sign-off-for-large-migrations answer is buried in section 6 of 9, and the question deliberately avoids 'migration'/'table' so only generic words carry the match. Today whole-document BM25 gets this wrong: standards/code-review (score 4.86, its own 'approving review' language) outranks the long runbook (4.45, rank 2) even though code-review's two-approver rule is scoped to auth/billing/data-deletion changes, not migrations — length dilution, not correctness, decides the top hit.

questions.question: can I rename a column and change its type in one release?
questions.probes: section-level retrieval: the specific answer (never rename and retype together; split into three releases) is in section 8 of 9. Today it still ranks 1st (score 5.89) but decisions/schema-evolution — a genuinely different concept about Avro field renames — trails closely at 5.50 on shared 'rename'/'type' vocabulary; length normalization has already eaten most of the long runbook's advantage.

questions.question: what should I keep an eye on for the first hour after a risky deploy?
questions.probes: section-level retrieval: the monitoring answer (replication lag, lock wait metrics for the first hour) is the final section of 9, and the question avoids 'migration'/'database' so it can't win on a title-field match. Today whole-document BM25 misses it entirely: it ranks 3rd (score 3.61) behind standards/code-review (4.52) and notes/query-cheatsheet (4.47), neither of which actually answers a post-migration monitoring question — the buried section never gets enough weight to surface the concept that has the real answer.

questions.question: how do we stop passwords from ending up in git?
questions.probes: paraphrase: the document never says password or git, only credential and repository — lexical search is expected to miss this entirely, and it does. Today it is not in the top 5 at all; the top hits (decisions/streaming-platform, gotchas/kafka-rebalance, decisions/service-stack...) share no real connection to secrets handling, they just match stray stopword-adjacent tokens. This documents a genuine synonym gap lexical ranking cannot close.

questions.question: how many people have to sign off before a change ships?
questions.probes: paraphrase: the document says approving review and approvals, never sign off or people — lexical search is expected to miss this, and it does. Today it is not in the top 5; runbooks/pre-launch-checklist, runbooks/database-migration-guide and runbooks/service-launch-approval rank above it purely because their own sign-off/approval language happens to overlap, not because they answer the question.

questions.question: how quickly do we have to write up a bad outage?
questions.probes: paraphrase: the document says postmortem, Sev1/Sev2, and blameless, never write up or outage — lexical search is expected to miss this, and it does. Today it is not in the top 5 at all; nothing in the top hits (runbooks/database-migration-guide, decisions/streaming-platform, notes/local-dev...) is a real answer, which is the honest measure of what lexical ranking leaves on the table here.

questions.question: what's our DB pick for new services?
questions.probes: paraphrase: abbreviation (DB) vs the document's spelled-out database/PostgreSQL/datastore; also colloquial pick vs default — lexical search is expected to miss this, and it does. Today it is not in the top 5; decisions/service-stack and runbooks/new-service-onboarding rank above it purely on the literal words 'new service(s)', never touching what database to use.

questions.question: who do I ask to get into prod for a bit?
questions.probes: paraphrase: prod vs production (abbreviation), ask vs requested, for a bit vs time-boxed — no shared stems with the document's actual wording. Lexical search is expected to miss this, and it does: today it is not in the top 5, with runbooks/deploy-standard and runbooks/new-service-onboarding ranking above it on unrelated 'production'-adjacent words rather than access control.
